item.title: How can that be profitable for Frito-Lay?: The Tipline for 19 February 2026
item.description: Retailers accusing Frito-Lay of price discrimination will not have the opportunity to challenge the merits of the promotional payments and discounts offered to supermarket chains. A federal California judge has struck down the case before discovery, finding that a class action is not the appropriate vehicle for a Robinson-Patman case. item.title: Law firm DEI programme suspended amid FTC scrutiny
item.description: An initiative encouraging law firms to interview a diverse talent pool has been suspended after the Federal Trade Commission sent warning letters to many of its participants.

item.title: Practitioners warn against “radical” California bill
item.description: California’s consideration of legislation to expand antitrust liability involving unilateral conduct would deviate from federal law and create uncertainty for local businesses, several competition experts have said.

item.title: Career growth: The Briefing for 20 February 2026
item.description: Doug Gurr has dug in, cementing his position as acting chair of the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority on a permanent basis. The CMA is yet to comment on the appointment, but it follows a government job advert last year that required the successful candidate to understand the importance of growth. item.title: Schlumberger faces Norwegian merger notification penalty over ChampionX
item.description: The Norwegian Competition Authority is seeking to fine Schlumberger €2.66 million for providing incorrect information on key tender rankings and products used in drilling services as part of its formal notification for its $7.8 billion takeover of ChampionX.

item.title: Meta’s WhatsApp AI policy faces fresh antitrust scrutiny
item.description: The Competition Commission of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa has joined several other antitrust agencies in probing Meta’s exclusion of rival AI chatbots from WhatsApp, but stopped short of issuing an interim injunction to suspend the new terms.

item.title: Alford to produce docs in HPE matter
item.description: A California federal judge has said Roger Alford must hand over communications related to Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s settlement with the Department of Justice, including those from after his firing from the agency.

item.title: DOJ sues OhioHealth for restricting narrower health plans
item.description: The Department of Justice has accused one of Ohio’s leading healthcare systems of using its market power to prohibit health insurers from offering cheaper plans to patients.

item.title: Everybody talks: The Tipline for 20 February 2026
item.description: It started with a whisper. Live Nation thinks the summary judgment ruling — which allowed most of the Department of Justice’s case to continue but axed key claims related to major concert venues — doomed its bid for a Ticketmaster divestiture. “It’s time to move on,” wrote in-house counsel Dan Wall in a blog post. item.title: FTC only seeking to block mergers in federal court, Ferguson says
item.description: Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson has signalled the agency will only fight pending mergers in federal court, a change that aligns its merger challenge process with the Department of Justice following years of legal challenges.
